record.original_question: For a given closed subgroup H of GL(n, R), is there a general criterion that decides whether an n-manifold admits an integrable H-structure, rather than only case-by-case criteria for special geometric structures such as almost complex, symplectic, or foliation-type structures?

evidence.quote: Problem 9, attributed to E. Calabi, asks for a general criterion to determine whether a manifold Mn admits an integrable H-structure, for some given closed subgroup H subset GL(n, R).

As explained in [Hi87], many important cases of this problem have been resolved, but the methods and techniques used are very different in the different cases, suggesting that the general formulation attempted by Calabi may in fact not be appropriate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H \subseteq GL(n,\mathbb{R})$ be a closed subgroup. An $H$-structure on a smooth $n$-manifold $M^n$ is a reduction of the structure group of the frame bundle $F(M) \to M$ from $GL(n,\mathbb{R})$ to $H$, i.e., a principal $H$-subbundle $P \subseteq F(M)$. Such an $H$-structure is called integrable if every point of $M$ has an open neighborhood $U$ together with local coordinates $(x^1, \dots, x^n)$ on $U$ such that the coordinate frame $(\partial/\partial x^1, \dots, \partial/\partial x^n)$ is a local section of $P$ over $U$ (equivalently, $P$ is locally equivalent, as an $H$-structure, to the standard flat $H$-structure on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Provide a general criterion, applicable to arbitrary closed subgroups $H \subseteq GL(n,\mathbb{R})$ and arbitrary smooth $n$-manifolds $M^n$, that determines whether $M$ admits an integrable $H$-structure. The criterion should be uniform in $H$, rather than tailored to particular geometric cases such as almost complex structures (with $H = GL(n/2,\mathbb{C})$), symplectic structures (with $H = Sp(n,\mathbb{R})$), or foliation structures.
artifact.status_search_result: The general integrability problem for $G$-structures (attributed to Calabi) has been resolved in many particular cases (almost complex, symplectic, foliations, etc.), each by different methods (e.g., Newlander–Nirenberg, Spencer cohomology, Guillemin's formal integrability theory). However, no uniform criterion applicable to arbitrary closed subgroups $H \subseteq GL(n,\mathbb{R})$ is known, and contemporary expositions suggest that such a uniform formulation may not be appropriate. The problem appears to remain open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Integrability of G-structures (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses integrability of G-structures with case-specific results (almost complex via Newlander-Nirenberg, etc.) without a unified criterion.
status_evidence.claim: Integrability is treated case-by-case for different subgroups G of GL(n,R).

status_evidence.title: The Integrability Problem for G-Structures, V. Guillemin
status_evidence.snippet: Guillemin develops formal/cohomological obstructions (Spencer cohomology) to integrability of G-structures.
status_evidence.claim: Formal integrability theory yields necessary conditions but not a complete general criterion.

status_evidence.title: A generalized integrability problem for G-structures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalizations of integrability for specific classes of G-structures, indicating the problem is still actively investigated.
status_evidence.claim: The general integrability question continues to be a research topic without a universal answer.
